purpose: A no-backend generator for permanent (static) QR codes — pick a type (Link/Text/WiFi/Phone/Email), type into the fields, watch a canvas preview redraw on every keystroke, then download PNG (512/1024/2048px) or SVG; nothing is stored, nothing is sent, no persistence at all.
structure: Single short page, no scrolling nav, no modals. body > div.wrap containing: (1) header.app — 32px icon.svg with alt="" (index.html:778), h1 "QR Maker" (779), span.spacer (780), a#tipLink.tipbtn.hidden un-hidden by JS (781); (2) div.hero — h2 "QR codes that never expire" + one marketing p (784-788); (3) section.card #1 — div.seg#typeSeg[role=tablist][aria-label="Code type"] (791, EMPTY in source, filled by JS) then div#fields (792, EMPTY in source, filled by JS). This card has NO h2 and no accessible name; (4) section.card #2 — h2 "Your code" (796, rendered by the base as a 12px uppercase micro-label), div#qrWrap > canvas#qrCanvas width=300 height=300 (797), p.hint#emptyHint (798), div.row with inline style="margin-top:10px" holding label.f[style="flex:0 0 130px"] > select#pngSize and label.f > select#ecLevel (799-812), div.row holding button#dlPng.btn.primary and button#dlSvg.btn (813-816), p.promise (817). Outside .wrap: div#toast[role=status][aria-live=polite] (821) and footer.colophon with two links carrying inline style="color:inherit" (822). Scripts: vendor-qrcode.js as a classic script exposing the global qrcode(), then app.js as a module (824-825). There is NO <main>, NO skip link, NO <noscript>. Flow: init() (app.js:164) wires buttons, reveals the tip link, calls renderFields() then update(); every keystroke calls update() (app.js:56) which rebuilds the payload, encodes, and repaints the canvas synchronously — no debounce.
cssClasses: header.app .tagline — subtitle under h1; SHIPPED BUT UNUSED here (283)
#tipLink — the tipbtn instance; JS sets href + drops .hidden (app.js:167-169)
.card .sub — 15px sub-line under a card heading; UNUSED (368)
#fields — unstyled container the field markup is injected into (792)
#emptyHint — the .hint carrying the only onboarding sentence (798)
#qrWrap — APP LAYER: white centered well, padding 14px, radius 12px (769)
#toast — fixed bottom pill, hidden by opacity+visibility (629)
.skip — skip-to-content link; SHIPPED BUT UNUSED, no target exists (687)
.empty / .glyph / h3 / p — empty-state component; UNUSED but badly needed (578-599)
.well — inset preview surface; UNUSED (#qrWrap reinvents it) (371)
.trust / .trust svg / .trust b — privacy stamp; UNUSED despite the pitch (331)
.tablewrap / table / th / td — scrollable table; UNUSED (605-625)
dynamicMarkup:
Two containers are empty in source and entirely JS-built, so a restyle that only reads index.html sees none of this markup. (A) #typeSeg — renderTypeSeg() (app.js:42-51) calls seg.replaceChildren() then appends 5 buttons: `` for the selected one and `` etc. for the rest. CRITICAL: non-active buttons get class="" — there is NO `.tab` class on any of them. They are styled ONLY by the descendant selector `.seg button` (index.html:502) and the state by `.seg button.active` (517). If the overhaul moves segmented-control styling to `.seg .tab` / `.seg .tab.is-active` and drops the bare-element selector, all five type buttons render as raw unstyled browser buttons. No aria-selected is ever set. (B) #fields — renderFields() (app.js:60-95) calls box.replaceChildren() then appends, per type: - url: `` - text: `` - wifi: `` + `` + conditionally `` (type=text, NOT password — the value is on screen and prints) + `

Guests point their camera at the code and join…

` - tel: `` - email: `` CRITICAL: every generated input, textarea and select carries NO class. They are styled purely by the element/attribute selectors at index.html:383-410 (`input[type=text]`, `input[type=url]`, `input[type=tel]`, `input[type=email]`, `select`, `textarea`). A restyle that switches control styling to classes (`.input`, `.select`, `.control`) leaves 100% of this app's form controls unstyled — 16px min font-size gone means iOS zooms on focus, 44px min-height gone means sub-target fields. Keep the element selectors, or teach app.js the new class names. (C) Class toggles at runtime: `.active` on seg buttons (app.js:47); `.hidden` on #emptyHint (app.js:116, 125, 133) and #tipLink (169); `.show` on #toast (26, 28). Renaming `.hidden`, `.show` or `.active` silently breaks behaviour with no error. (D) Canvas mutation: update() (app.js:107-136) and drawQrToCanvas() (helpers.js:55-69) write canvas.width / canvas.height as raw attributes — 300x300 on the empty and error paths (app.js:113-114, 130-131), and `cell * (moduleCount + 8)` on the success path (helpers.js:59-61), which is a data-dependent number (e.g. 296, 290, 285) that changes as the user types. (E) Transient anchor: download() (app.js:138-143) appends a bare `` to document.body, clicks it, and removes it 300ms later. A new global `a{}` display/layout rule or a `body > *:last-child` rule can make it flash on screen. (F) el() helper (app.js:7-21): key `class` sets className, key `text` sets textContent, keys starting `on` become addEventListener. Anything else becomes setAttribute. There is no place to hook a class prefix — restyling means editing these call sites.

comfortDefects.issue: The type selector — the app's primary control — has 38px-tall targets, 6px under the system's own --tap:44px, with only a 4px gap between adjacent targets. On a 320px phone the five tabs wrap to two rows of 38px.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:502-505 (.seg button{min-height:38px}) instanced at index.html:791 / app.js:46
comfortDefects.fix: min-height:var(--tap) on .seg button, or 40px with --s2 gap. If the row gets too tall on mobile, switch the .seg to a 2-column grid rather than shrinking the target.

comfortDefects.issue: .promise hardcodes font-size:.85rem (13.6px) and margin-top:6px, bypassing both the type scale and the 4px spacing scale, and reaches for the legacy --muted alias instead of --ink-2.
comfortDefects.fix: font-size:var(--t-xs); margin-top:var(--s2); color:var(--ink-2). Better: promote it to the unused .trust component — this sentence is the app's whole value proposition and it is currently the smallest text on the page.

comfortDefects.issue: .promise is text-align:center but inherits p{max-width:var(--measure)} with no margin-inline:auto, so its 64ch box is left-aligned inside the ~592px card and the centred sentence sits ~70px left of the QR code it sits under. Visibly off-axis on any screen wider than ~470px.
comfortDefects.fix: add margin-inline:auto (or max-width:none) to .promise. Audit every other centred p in the portfolio for the same base-rule collision.

comfortDefects.issue: #qrWrap paints a hardcoded #fff and in dark mode becomes a ~300px pure-white slab at 21:1 against the #10160f page — a glare block for the exact night-time phone use this app invites ("stick it on the fridge").
comfortDefects.fix: Keep the canvas ground white (scanners need it, and helpers.js paints white into the bitmap anyway) but inset it: give #qrWrap a --surface-2 frame with generous padding and only the canvas itself white, or dim the wrap to ~#e8e8e8 in dark mode. Do NOT tint the canvas.

comfortDefects.issue: #qrWrap uses padding:14px and border-radius:12px — neither is on the scale, and 12px contradicts this skin's --r:8px, so the QR well is rounder than every card around it.
comfortDefects.fix: padding:var(--s4); border-radius:var(--r-ctl). Then it tracks the skin when --r changes.

comfortDefects.issue: The onboarding sentence — the single line telling a first-time user what to do — is 13px --ink-2 helper text tucked under a blank white square.
comfortDefects.fix: Replace with the unused .empty component (index.html:578-599): glyph, --t-lg h3, and 15px body. It is already in the stylesheet and costs nothing.

comfortDefects.issue: Multi-line body copy runs at line-height 1.35 (--lh-snug), under the 1.45 comfort floor. The WiFi explainer is ~190 characters at 13px/1.35 — three to four tight lines.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:524-529 (.hint) applied to the paragraph built at app.js:87
comfortDefects.fix: Give .hint line-height:var(--lh-body) when it holds a sentence; reserve --lh-snug for single-line labels. Or raise .hint to --t-sm (15px).

comfortDefects.issue: Cold open shows an unlabelled blank white 300x300 rectangle. It reads as a broken image or a stalled loader, not as "nothing to show yet".
comfortDefects.where: app.js:110-118 (empty path fills the canvas white) rendered into index.html:797
comfortDefects.fix: Hide #qrWrap entirely while currentQr is null and show the .empty block in its place; swap back on first successful encode.

comfortDefects.issue: image-rendering:pixelated plus a data-dependent backing store. drawQrToCanvas sizes the bitmap to cell*(modules+8) — e.g. 296px — and on a 320px viewport the CSS box is only ~220px after .wrap(16)+card(20)+qrWrap(14) gutters, a 1.35x non-integer downscale. Nearest-neighbour then renders modules at uneven widths, which is the classic cause of a preview that will not scan.
comfortDefects.fix: Render the preview at an integer multiple of the module count times devicePixelRatio and set an explicit CSS width that is an integer multiple, or use image-rendering:auto below the 1:1 threshold. This is a scanning-correctness issue, not only comfort.

comfortDefects.issue: Field labels and all helper text sit at --t-xs (13px) while body copy scales up to 17px above 30rem — so on desktop the gap between prose and the labels people actually read while typing gets wider, not narrower.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:218 (body font-size bump) vs index.html:416-422 (label.f > span) and 524 (.hint)
comfortDefects.fix: Move field labels to --t-sm (15px) and give .hint/.small the same rem-scaling treatment as body, or drop the body bump so the ratio stays constant.

comfortDefects.issue: Magic numbers in the markup: style="margin-top:10px" and style="flex:0 0 130px". The second pins the PNG-size field to 130px, which after the select's 32px caret gutter leaves ~85px for "1024 px" plus the caret — tight at large text sizes and it cannot respond to a new type scale.
comfortDefects.fix: Delete both. Use .frow (index.html:425) for the two-select row and let flex:1 1 9rem do the work.

comfortDefects.issue: The second .row (download buttons) carries no top margin of its own; the only separation from the selects above is label.f's margin-bottom. Delete or restructure a label and the buttons collide with the selects.
comfortDefects.fix: Wrap both rows in .stack, or give the button row an explicit margin-top:var(--s5) so its spacing does not depend on a sibling's bottom margin.

comfortDefects.issue: #pngSize and #ecLevel are visually identical selects side by side, but changing toughness re-renders the live preview while changing PNG size does nothing visible at all — the user cannot tell which control is live.
comfortDefects.where: index.html:799-812; #ecLevel is wired at app.js:146, #pngSize is only read at app.js:150
comfortDefects.fix: Add a .hint under PNG size ("applies to the downloaded file") and move it beside the Download PNG button rather than next to the live control.

comfortDefects.issue: The two download buttons are equal-width via .row > *{flex:1 1 12rem}, so primary and secondary read as the same weight and only the fill colour distinguishes them — no size, order or grouping hierarchy.
comfortDefects.fix: Use .cluster instead of .row so buttons size to content, and give #dlPng .btn.big. Consider parking both in the unused .actionbar so they stay reachable.

comfortDefects.issue: Every keystroke triggers a full QR encode and canvas repaint with no debounce, while body carries a fixed-attachment 26px grid texture — on iOS the combination causes visible repaint jank while typing a long text payload.
comfortDefects.fix: requestAnimationFrame-coalesce or 120ms-debounce update(); consider dropping background-attachment:fixed on touch devices.

navigationDefects.issue: No empty state. Opened cold the page offers a blank white square, an unlabelled tab strip and one 13px line. The .empty component that would teach the flow is in the stylesheet and unused.
navigationDefects.fix: Show an .empty block inside #qrWrap while currentQr is null: glyph, "Your code appears here", "Pick a type above and start typing."

navigationDefects.issue: The user never sees what will actually be encoded. buildPayload silently prepends https:// to anything without a recognised scheme — 'www.example.com' becomes 'https://www.example.com', and 'javascript:alert(1)' becomes the nonsense 'https://javascript:alert(1)'. On an app whose entire pitch is "print this on 500 menus, it works forever", there is no way to verify the payload before committing it to paper.
navigationDefects.where: helpers.js:16 (rewrite) with no readout anywhere in index.html or app.js
navigationDefects.fix: Render the final payload string under the code in a .well with monospace and a Copy button. This is the single highest-value addition to the app.

navigationDefects.issue: Download buttons look fully enabled with no code present and only reveal the problem as a toast after the click.
navigationDefects.where: index.html:814-815; guard at app.js:148 and app.js:155
navigationDefects.fix: Set the disabled property on both when currentQr is null (the base already styles :disabled at index.html:412). Keep the toast as the fallback.

navigationDefects.issue: Nothing tells the user that nothing is saved. There is no localStorage anywhere in the app — a reload or an accidental back-swipe silently destroys a typed WiFi SSID and password with no warning and no restore.
navigationDefects.where: whole of app.js — the `fields` object at app.js:39 is in-memory only
navigationDefects.fix: Either persist to localStorage with a visible "saved on this device only" note, or state the ephemerality up front ("Nothing is saved — download before you close this") near the download buttons. Silence is the worst of the three.

navigationDefects.issue: No clear / start-over. Switching type keeps every previous type's values alive in the fields map, so a WiFi password typed ten minutes ago is still live and still encodable, but is invisible until the user navigates back to that tab.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:39 and app.js:55 (keys are type+'.'+key, never cleared)
navigationDefects.fix: Add a .btn.ghost "Clear" that empties `fields` and re-renders, plus a subtle indicator on tabs that already hold data.

navigationDefects.issue: The WiFi password field is removed from the DOM when Security is set to Open, but fields['wifi.pass'] retains the value and it returns on switching back — invisible state the user cannot audit.
navigationDefects.fix: Either delete the key when auth becomes nopass, or keep the field visible and disabled so the retained value is honest.

navigationDefects.issue: No <noscript>. With JS blocked the page renders the hero, an empty tab strip, an empty fields div and a blank canvas — indistinguishable from a broken site.
navigationDefects.where: index.html:775-819 (no noscript anywhere); both containers empty in source at 791-792
navigationDefects.fix: Add a <noscript> .warn inside the first card: "This tool runs entirely in your browser and needs JavaScript on."

navigationDefects.issue: The input card has no heading at all, so there is no label over the app's primary work area and no anchor for anyone scanning the page by heading.
navigationDefects.where: index.html:790-793 (section.card with no h2, unlike the second card at 796)
navigationDefects.fix: Add an h2 ("What to encode") — the base renders it as the standard micro-label, matching "Your code".

navigationDefects.issue: On a phone the preview and download buttons sit below the fold while the user is typing, and there is no sticky element, scroll cue or in-page anchor. Typing feels like it produces nothing.
navigationDefects.fix: Put #dlPng/#dlSvg in the .actionbar so they stay pinned, or make #qrWrap position:sticky on narrow viewports.

navigationDefects.issue: The error path contradicts itself: an over-long payload clears the canvas and un-hides #emptyHint, so the page says "Start typing above" to a user who has just typed too much, while the real explanation is a toast that vanishes in 4 seconds.
navigationDefects.where: app.js:126-135 (catch block re-shows #emptyHint) vs the text at index.html:798
navigationDefects.fix: Give the overflow case its own persistent .warn message near the canvas; leave the toast for transient confirmations only.

navigationDefects.issue: No print button and no share path. The app's own copy tells people to print the code (index.html:817) and stick it on the fridge (app.js:87), but the only route to paper is download-then-open-elsewhere, and on iOS a downloaded PNG is several taps away.
navigationDefects.fix: Add a Print button that opens a purpose-built print layout, and use navigator.share/canShare with the PNG file where available.

navigationDefects.issue: The only way back to the rest of the studio is a link buried in the footer with its colour overridden to the lowest-contrast token on the page.
navigationDefects.fix: Drop the inline color:inherit so the base's footer.colophon a rule (index.html:325) applies, and consider a studio link in the header.

a11yDefects.issue: Broken tablist. #typeSeg declares role=tablist and JS gives all five buttons role=tab, but nothing sets aria-selected, aria-controls, tabindex or arrow-key handling, and #fields is not a tabpanel. A screen reader announces "tab" five times and never says which is current; the selected state exists only as the .active class. This is a worse experience than plain buttons.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:791 (role=tablist) and app.js:46-49 (role:'tab', class:'active', no ARIA state)
a11yDefects.fix: Cheapest correct fix: drop role=tab/tablist and use aria-pressed={true|false} toggle buttons in a group with aria-label. If the tab pattern is kept, add aria-selected, aria-controls="fields", id/aria-labelledby, role=tabpanel + tabindex="0" on #fields, roving tabindex, and Left/Right/Home/End key handling.

a11yDefects.issue: Focus is destroyed on every type switch. Clicking a type button calls renderFields() -> renderTypeSeg() -> seg.replaceChildren(), which removes the very button that has focus; focus falls to document.body. A keyboard user tabbing to "WiFi" and pressing Enter is dumped back at the top of the document.
a11yDefects.fix: Reuse the existing buttons and only toggle classes/aria-selected, or capture the index before replaceChildren() and re-focus the corresponding new button afterwards.

a11yDefects.issue: Focus is destroyed mid-interaction on the WiFi Security select. Its onchange calls renderFields(), which rebuilds the select as a brand-new node — so after choosing "Open (no password)" with the keyboard, focus is on body and the control the user was operating no longer exists.
a11yDefects.fix: Only add/remove the password label rather than rebuilding #fields, and restore focus to the select if a rebuild is unavoidable.

a11yDefects.issue: The canvas carries a static aria-label="Generated QR code" that never changes, and <canvas> has no implicit img role, so many screen readers drop the label entirely. The label says a code was generated even when the canvas is a blank white square.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:797; the label is never touched anywhere in app.js
a11yDefects.fix: Add role="img" and update the accessible name from update() to describe the actual payload — e.g. "QR code for https://example.com" or "No code yet".

a11yDefects.issue: No live region for the result. The code redraws and #emptyHint appears/disappears with pure class toggles, so a non-sighted user gets no signal that a valid code now exists or has just become invalid. #toast is a live region but only fires on the too-much-data error and on downloads.
a11yDefects.where: app.js:116, 125, 133 (classList toggles on #emptyHint) — no aria-live anywhere except index.html:821
a11yDefects.fix: Add a visually-hidden aria-live="polite" status element that announces "Code ready" / "Code cleared", debounced so it does not fire on every keystroke.

a11yDefects.issue: Footer body text fails contrast: --ink-3 #818d80 on --canvas #f3faf2 computes to 3.26:1 at 13px, well under 4.5:1. This is the text carrying the privacy promise ("we never see what you encode") — the app's core claim rendered in the least readable type on the page. Light mode only; dark mode is 5.06:1.
a11yDefects.fix: Use --ink-2 (5.58:1) for footer.colophon, or darken --ink-3 in the light skin to roughly #6b7569. This is a base-layer fix that improves all 23 apps.

a11yDefects.issue: Both footer links carry inline style="color:inherit", which beats the base's footer.colophon a{color:var(--ink-2)} rule and drags them down to the failing 3.26:1 --ink-3 value, while also removing the colour distinction between link and text (only the underline remains).
a11yDefects.fix: Delete both inline styles and let index.html:325-326 apply. Inline styles also silently defeat the overhaul's new link styling.

a11yDefects.issue: Placeholder text fails contrast: --ink-3 #818d80 on --field #f8fcf8 computes to 3.35:1. These placeholders are not decorative — they carry the format examples ('skywolf.example or https://…', '+1 555 010 1234', 'hello@example.com') that tell the user what shape of input is expected.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:401 (::placeholder{color:var(--ink-3)}) applied to the inputs generated at app.js:66, 90, 93
a11yDefects.fix: Use --ink-2 for ::placeholder, or better, move the format examples into visible .hint text under each label so they survive typing.

a11yDefects.issue: No <main> landmark and no skip link. The base ships a fully styled .skip component but the markup never uses it and there is no landmark target — landmark navigation offers only banner and contentinfo, with the entire app in an unlabelled region. This is a portfolio-wide gap: no app under apps/ contains <main> or class="skip".
a11yDefects.where: index.html:775-819 (no main, no skip anchor); unused CSS at index.html:687-696
a11yDefects.fix:
Wrap the two section.card blocks in
and add Skip to the tool as the first child of body.

a11yDefects.issue: Both containers whose contents are entirely replaced (#typeSeg and #fields) are plain divs with no aria-live and no focus management, so the wholesale DOM swap on every type change is completely silent to assistive tech.
a11yDefects.fix: Once the tab/panel relationship is correct, move focus into the panel after a switch (tabindex="-1" on the panel) so the new fields are announced.

a11yDefects.issue: The download buttons stay in the accessibility tree as ordinary enabled buttons when there is nothing to download, giving AT no indication that activating them cannot succeed.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:814-815 with the runtime-only guard at app.js:148 and app.js:155
a11yDefects.fix: Toggle the disabled property (or aria-disabled plus the existing :disabled styling at index.html:412) from update().

a11yDefects.issue: Focus ring geometry on the segmented control is fragile: :focus-visible draws a 2px outline at 2px offset, and .seg's own padding is exactly 4px, so the ring lands flush against the .seg border. On the active tab the ring colour --focus #3f8439 against the tab fill --accent-fill #367b30 is 1.13:1 — invisible. It only reads because the 2px offset pushes it onto --surface-2 (4.20:1). Any restyle that zeroes the offset, tightens .seg padding, or gives the seg overflow:hidden makes the selected tab's focus state disappear.
a11yDefects.where: index.html:669-673 (:focus-visible) against index.html:492-496 (.seg padding) and index.html:517-521 (.seg button.active)
a11yDefects.fix: Give .seg at least --s2 padding, and add an inner white/--surface ring (box-shadow inset) on .active:focus-visible so the indicator is legible on the accent fill regardless of offset.

printSupport:
There is a print block, but it is entirely the shared base layer (index.html:725-754) — this app adds ZERO print CSS of its own and has no Print button.

Is print a core use case? Yes, emphatically, and the app says so itself: index.html:817 "Print it as big as a billboard" and app.js:87 "Stick it on the fridge or frame it for the guest room." A QR code's normal destination is paper — a table tent, a flyer, a guest-room WiFi card, a shop window. Right now the only route to paper is Download PNG, open the file elsewhere, print from there.

What the base gives you: --canvas/--surface/--field forced to #fff, ink to #000, shadows off, body at 11pt, .wrap unwrapped, @page margin 14mm, and display:none on header.app, footer.colophon, .tipbtn, .actionbar, #toast, .seg, .skip, .noprint/.no-print/.screenonly.

What is broken today if a user just hits Cmd+P:
1. The tab strip vanishes (.seg is hidden at index.html:740) but #fields does not — so the printed page shows input boxes with no indication of what kind of code they describe.
2. The WiFi password prints in clear text. app.js:85 creates the password input as type="text", and form control values render in print. Print the WiFi page and you hand out the network password in a bordered box next to the code. This is a privacy defect, not just a layout one.
3. Both download buttons, the PNG-size select and the toughness select all print as dead controls. None carries .noprint.
4. The hero paragraph and .promise marketing copy print — roughly a third of the page is sales text.
5. The QR itself prints at ~300 CSS px (≈3.1 inch at 96dpi) from a ~296px backing store, so effective resolution is about 96dpi. That is at the low end of reliable scanning for a small code and visibly soft. image-rendering:pixelated (index.html:770) makes the module edges ragged rather than crisp in pipelines that honour it.
6. #qrWrap's border and 12px radius print around the code; a quiet zone plus a hairline box is fine, but the rounded corner on a scanning target is noise.
7. No print-only caption. A printed WiFi code with no visible SSID is useless to anyone whose camera fails; a printed link code with no visible URL is unverifiable.

What to add during the overhaul:
- A Print button next to the downloads.
- An app-level @media print that hides .hero, the two selects, both download buttons and .promise (add .noprint to them), and drops the #qrWrap border.
- A .printonly caption block under the code carrying the human-readable payload plus a type-appropriate line ("Scan to join <SSID>" / the URL as text), using the .printonly toggle the base already ships at index.html:742.
- Render the print image from the SVG path (helpers.js:41-53) rather than the canvas, or repaint the canvas at 4x with a print-resolution CSS width — the SVG is resolution-independent and is the right source for paper.
- Consider a dedicated "WiFi card" print layout: SSID, code, and "Scan to join" centred on one page. That is a real artifact people want and it is maybe 30 lines of CSS.
- Never print the password unless the user opts in.
riskyToRestyle: Canvas sizing is JS-owned and data-dependent. drawQrToCanvas (helpers.js:55-61) sets canvas.width/height to cell*(moduleCount+8) — a number that changes as the user types (296, 290, 285…) — and app.js:113-114 / 130-131 reset both to 300 on the empty and error paths. The width="300" height="300" attributes at index.html:797 are only the initial value. NEVER set a fixed pixel width/height on #qrCanvas in CSS: any non-uniform scale distorts the modules and can make the code unscannable. If you must control display size, set width and leave height:auto (as index.html:770 does today).

image-rendering:pixelated (index.html:770) is scan-critical, not aesthetic. Removing it softens module edges; keeping it while the CSS box is a non-integer fraction of the bitmap produces uneven module widths. Whichever you choose, verify by scanning the preview on a phone at 320px width — this is the one visual property in the app that has a functional failure mode.

Never theme the QR itself. The exported artifacts hardcode black on white in two places: helpers.js:63-64 (ctx.fillStyle '#fff' then '#000') and helpers.js:51-52 (the SVG <rect fill="#ffffff"> and <path fill="#000000">). #qrWrap's background:#fff (index.html:769) must stay light. Do not apply filter, opacity, mix-blend-mode, background-blend-mode or an accent tint to #qrWrap or #qrCanvas — inverted or low-contrast codes fail on a large share of scanners, and a downloaded file that does not match the on-screen preview is worse still.

All runtime form controls are class-less and styled only by element/attribute selectors (index.html:383-410). app.js:53-58, 68, 73-77 create bare input/textarea/select nodes. If the overhaul moves to class-based control styling, every field in this app loses its 44px min-height and its 16px min font-size — which means iOS Safari starts zooming the page on focus. Either keep the element selectors in the base, or update the five construction sites in app.js in the same commit.

Segmented-control buttons carry class="active" or class="" and nothing else (app.js:47). They depend on the bare descendant selectors .seg button and .seg button.active (index.html:502, 517). Introducing .tab / .is-active / .seg__item naming without editing app.js leaves five unstyled native buttons as the app's primary control.

Class names the JS toggles: .hidden (app.js:116, 125, 133, 169), .show (app.js:26, 28), .active (app.js:47), plus .f and .hint applied at app.js:65, 71, 80, 82, 84, 87, 89, 92. Renaming any of these in CSS breaks behaviour silently — no console error, just a permanently visible hint or an invisible tip jar. .hidden{display:none !important} (index.html:699) must keep its !important, because #tipLink also carries .tipbtn{display:inline-flex}.

IDs the JS reaches for by getElementById: toast, typeSeg, fields, qrCanvas, emptyHint, ecLevel, pngSize, dlPng, dlSvg, tipLink (app.js:6 and throughout). Adding wrapper elements around them is safe; renaming or removing any is a hard break. #typeSeg additionally must remain the direct ARIA parent of the role=tab buttons — wrapping each button in a div severs the tablist/tab ownership.

Four inline style attributes beat any new stylesheet rule without !important: index.html:799 (margin-top:10px), 800 (flex:0 0 130px), and two occurrences of color:inherit at 822. The last pair actively overrides the base's own footer link colour and drops it to a failing 3.26:1. Strip all four as the first step of the overhaul.

The stylesheet is generated and spliced. Everything between the markers at index.html:18 ("▼▼▼ SWS STUDIO BASE") and index.html:766 ("▲▲▲ END SWS STUDIO BASE ▲▲▲") is written by design/apply.mjs from design/studio.css + design/skins.mjs (this app's skin is at design/skins.mjs:175-179: hue 142, chroma 0.13, r 8, wrap 40rem, texture grid). Hand-edits inside the markers are destroyed on the next build. App-specific rules must stay below index.html:768.

Palette colours are duplicated in five files outside the stylesheet and will drift: index.html:12-13 (two theme-color metas, #f3faf2 / #10160f), manifest.webmanifest (background_color #f3faf2, theme_color #367b30), icon.svg:2 (rect fill #367b30, baked rx="14" that fights the base's border-radius:var(--r-sm)=4px at the 32px render size in index.html:277), and marketing/stripe-thumbnail.png + marketing/thumb-256.png. A skin change must touch all of them.

The service worker will serve stale CSS after deploy. sw.js:3 lists a fixed ASSETS array and sw.js:20 is cache-first (`return cached || fetched`), so returning users get the OLD index.html on the first load after a deploy and only pick up the new design on the second. If the overhaul adds an external stylesheet or a new font file, it must be appended to ASSETS AND VERSION bumped from 'qr-v5' (sw.js:2) or those files are never fetched at all offline.

Tests give you no safety net here. test/helpers.test.mjs asserts only on helpers.js pure functions — payload strings, WiFi escaping, and the SVG output shape (startsWith '<svg', includes 'crispEdges', length > 500, and the exact viewBox="0 0 N+8 N+8" quiet-zone at test/helpers.test.mjs:51). Nothing touches the DOM, class names or the stylesheet, so a restyle cannot break the suite — and equally, the suite cannot catch a restyle regression. Do not 'clean up' the SVG string in helpers.js:50-52 (whitespace, attribute order, adding a theme colour) — those three assertions are the only automated guard in the app.
